data.title: The minimal number of transfers and the explanation of the calculation

events.line: Accepted, I will study the code and write the statement of task 2
events.text:
Write the statement of task 2 from the series for the split-bill project. Task 1 (the skeleton) is already done and committed, read the code yourself.

Task: calculating the debts with the minimal number of transfers. An algorithm with tests for the edge cases is needed: one paid for everyone, mutual debts, kopecks and rounding, zero expenses. The interface needs a clear explanation of the calculation. The "Share" link and the mobile layout with the README are the next tasks, do not include them in this one.

The human's decisions are made in advance: the statement is approved, resolve the forks yourself and put them into the section "Accepted decisions". The minimum of transfers in the general case is a hard problem of splitting into the largest number of groups with a zero sum. Decide how to solve it: for example, an exact search over subsets for a small group and a correct fallback for large ones. Name the limit as a constant and describe what happens beyond it. The result must be deterministic.

The explanation of the calculation is for an ordinary person, without formulas and jargon: how much was spent in total, how much each one paid and how much they spent, their outcome ("is owed", "owes" or "settled") and why there are this many transfers. Choose a simple format that can be read at a glance.

Required tests: one paid for everyone; mutual debts that cancel out; kopecks and rounding, the sum of the transfers adds up to the kopeck; zero expenses; a case where the greedy algorithm gives more transfers than the minimum. Follow the project rules. Name what does not belong to the task in the section "Out of scope".

events.line: Here is the statement: exact search and the breakdown of the calculation
events.text:
The statement is ready. Goal: the summary shows the smallest possible number of transfers, and next to it an explanation for an ordinary person: how much was spent in total, how much each one paid, what their share is, what their outcome is and why there are exactly this many transfers.

Accepted decisions. The minimum is found like this: the transfers needed are n minus g, where n is the number of participants with a non-zero balance and g is the largest number of zero-sum groups they can be split into. g is found by an exact search over subsets, inside each group the former greedy pass works. The limit of the exact search is 16 participants with a non-zero balance, beyond that the calculation stops being instant. If there are more such participants, a fallback works: a greedy pass over all, it is correct and gives at most n minus 1 transfers, but does not guarantee the minimum; the result marks this with a flag, and the interface honestly says so. The result is deterministic: among equal options the participant with the smaller number is taken, transfers are sorted by debtor, then by recipient. A non-zero sum of balances is a contract error, the calculation throws an exception. How much was paid and what the share is are counted in the domain logic, the balance outcome is computed in one place. The wording does not depend on gender, declension goes through Intl.PluralRules. The note about kopecks is shown only if there is an expense that does not divide evenly.

Plan: add counting the total of the expenses and a check of uneven division; extend the balance with the fields paid and share; rewrite the transfer calculation (exact group search, greedy pass inside groups, sorting, the limit as a constant); add declension of numerals and a module with the explanation texts; in the summary section show the transfers, the phrase "why this many" and the block "How it is calculated" with a row per participant and notes; add the minimum of styles, do not touch the mobile layout.

Done criteria: make check is green; for balances 300, 200, minus 200, minus 300 exactly two transfers come out, although the greedy one gave three; one paid for three — two transfers of 300 rubles; mutual 500 for 500 — no transfers, 700 for 300 — one transfer of 400 rubles; 100 rubles for three — shares 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33, the sum of the transfers adds up to the kopeck; after the transfers all balances are zero; zero expenses — only the hint without the block "How it is calculated"; exactly at the limit and one above the limit the behavior is checked; the result repeats, the input data does not change. In the interface for "Ann paid 900 for three" the total, the rows per participant and the phrase about two transfers are visible. For "Ann 300 for Ben, Clara 200 for Eve" the phrase starts with "2 transfers instead of 3".

The tests lie next to the code and cover all the listed cases, as well as declension, the explanation texts and the interface scenarios.

Out of scope: the "Share" link, the mobile layout, the README and Pages. Noticed on the way and not fixed: the aria-live area hangs on the whole summary section, and a screen reader will read a lot of text on every change.

events.line: Accepted. I do the exact search, the breakdown and the tests
events.text:
Do task 2 of the split-bill project by the approved statement. Task 1 (the skeleton) is already committed. Do not commit — the lead will do it. First read the project rules: names from the domain, no magic values, immutability of the input, one function — one action, nesting no deeper than two, an intermediate result gets a name, no more than one nested call in a call argument, texts and comments in Russian, identifiers in English.

The content of the statement: the summary shows the smallest number of transfers, and next to it goes an explanation for an ordinary person. The minimum is n minus g, where g is found by an exact search over subsets with a greedy pass inside the groups; the limit of the search is 16 participants with a non-zero balance, beyond it a greedy fallback with a flag that the minimum is not guaranteed. The result is deterministic, a non-zero sum of balances is an exception. The balance gets the fields paid and share, added are the total of the expenses, a check of uneven division, declension of numerals, the explanation texts and the block "How it is calculated" in the summary. The done criteria and the list of tests are given in the statement.

The lead's correction: in the second branch of the phrase about the number of transfers, when there are fewer transfers than usual, the text is this — "{t} instead of the usual {n−1}: {n} people give or receive money, but they split into groups that settle among themselves. It can't be fewer." Accordingly, for "Ann 300 for Ben, Clara 200 for Eve" the phrase starts with "2 transfers instead of the usual 3: 4 people give or receive money".

At the end run the formatting and make check, it must be green. In the answer write what was done by the points of the plan, what deviations there were and why, and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here you are. Task 2 is ready, make check is green, 127 tests
events.text:
Task 2 is done. After formatting make check is green: types, linter, 127 tests in eight files and the build. Nothing is committed.

By the points of the plan. Added are the counting of the total of the expenses and the check of uneven division, both with tests. The fields "paid" and "share" are added to the balance, they are collected in one pass, and the balance outcome is computed in one place only; the expectations in the tests are moved to the new fields. The transfer calculation is rewritten: the limit of the exact search is 16 with a comment, the result has a minimality flag, the top level only names the steps. Separately extracted are the search of zero-sum groups (subset sums in a floating-point array, the number of groups in an integer one), the greedy pass on a copy of the positions and the sorting. Among equal options the smaller index is taken, a non-zero sum gives an exception. The tests cover all cases from the criteria. Added are the declension of numerals and the module of the explanation texts with three variants of the phrase about the number of transfers, the second branch is written by the lead's correction. The summary section collects the transfers, the phrase "why this many" and the block "How it is calculated"; without expenses only the hint is shown. Styles for the notes are added, I did not touch the mobile layout. New interface tests: the breakdown for "one for everyone", the phrase about the number of transfers, mutual debts, the note about kopecks, the "instead of the usual" variant on four participants, the absence of the block without expenses.

Deviations: the choice between the exact and the fallback variant is written as one conditional expression with shared sorting and flag, not as two returns, the behavior is the same; the group search takes and returns balances, not indices, so that the calling code does not need checks for a missing value. To keep nesting no deeper than two levels, helper functions are extracted.

Noticed and not touched: the aria-live area hangs on the whole summary section, and now screen readers will read a lot of text on every change. The statement told not to fix it.

events.line: Accepted. I will check the minimum, the speed, the determinism
events.text:
Review the uncommitted changes for task 2: calculating the debts with the minimal number of transfers with a clear explanation in the interface. Task 1 was committed earlier, review only task 2. Experiments that break the code do in a copy in a temporary directory, not in the working copy. Do not change files.

The key decisions of the statement: the minimum equals n minus g, where g is the largest number of zero-sum groups found by an exact search over subsets, inside a group a greedy pass; the search limit is 16 non-zero balances, beyond it a greedy one over all with a flag that the minimum is not guaranteed; determinism; a non-zero sum of balances is an exception; the balance has the fields "paid" and "share"; the explanation with transfers, the phrase "why this many" and the block "How it is calculated"; declension through Intl.PluralRules; the wording does not depend on gender.

Done criteria: make check is green; balances 300, 200, minus 200, minus 300 give exactly two transfers; one paid for three — two transfers of 300 rubles; mutual debts 500 for 500 cancel out, 700 for 300 give one transfer of 400; kopecks and 100 rubles for three add up to the kopeck; after the transfers the balances are zero, every transfer is positive and between different people; zero expenses — only the hint; the behavior exactly at the limit and one above; a repeated call gives the same result, a frozen input does not change; the interface shows the total, the rows per participant and the needed phrases.

Assess the executor's deviations: the conditional expression for choosing between the exact and the fallback variant, the group search on balances instead of indices, the extracted helper functions.

Check especially the correctness of the search: whether the minimum is really found, whether there are precision problems when comparing subset sums in a floating-point array and whether the complexity turned out worse than O(2ⁿ·n). Measure the speed on 16 non-zero balances, check determinism and the project rules: names of intermediate results, nesting up to two, no magic values, one function — one action. The texts must be clear to an ordinary person.

events.line: Accepted: the minimum is right, small remarks do not block
events.text:
ACCEPTED. There are no serious remarks. make check is green: types, linter, 127 tests and the build, the formatter gave no remarks. I did not change the working copy, all experiments went in a copy.

What was checked separately. The minimum is found correctly: I compared the calculation with an independent reference on 3000 random sets of 2 to 10 balances, the number of transfers matched everywhere, and the balances after the transfers become zero. The complexity is O(2ⁿ·n), not O(3ⁿ): the group recovery goes along the same chain as the counting, so the found groups give exactly the needed number. The precision of the floating-point array is sufficient, it holds sums of whole kopecks, exact up to 2 to the power of 53; checked on large values, and an integer array would not fit here because of overflow. On 16 non-zero balances the worst case took about 17 milliseconds, which is enough for recalculation on every render. The result is deterministic. All done criteria are met and covered by tests. The executor's deviations are justified. There are no secrets or personal data in the changes.

Small remarks, they do not block. The interface itself counts the number of participants in the calculation, although the same concept exists in the algorithm — the rule of one source of truth is broken. The array of notes is filled through push, but it can be set by a conditional expression. The phrase about the extra kopeck can be understood as "they will be charged extra", it is more precise to say that the share is a kopeck larger for those higher in the list. In the calculation of the lowest bit number there is the number 31 without a name. The check of uneven division repeats the rule from the division function, but they are in one file. The phrase "it can't be fewer" explains why n minus 1 transfers are enough, but not why fewer is impossible. The tests lack a comparison of the minimum with random sets and checks of the format "33,33 ₽" and "400,00 ₽" at the interface level.

events.line: Accepted. I will make the reviewer's six small fixes
events.text:
Rework task 2 of the split-bill project. The changes lie uncommitted in the working copy. The review accepted the task, and the lead asks to make the reviewer's small fixes before the checks. Read the project rules, do not commit and change nothing beyond the listed.

The first fix: the concept "takes part in the calculation" must live in one place in the domain logic. Now the interface itself counts the number of participants in the calculation with a filter by non-zero balance, although the same concept exists in the transfer calculation. For example, give the transfer plan a field with this number or extract a shared predicate. Choose what reads easier and update the tests.

The second: the array of notes in the summary section is filled through push, make it immutably with one conditional expression.

The third: make the note text about kopecks clearer — "When an expense doesn't split evenly to the kopeck, those higher in the participant list get a share one kopeck larger."

The fourth: the number 31 in the calculation of the lowest bit number must have a name, for example a separate function or a constant with a comment on "why".

The fifth: the third branch of the phrase about the number of transfers explains why n−1 transfers are enough, but not why fewer is impossible. The new text: "{t} — it can't be fewer: {n} people give or receive money, and when they can't be split into groups that settle among themselves, you need one transfer fewer than there are people." The beginning of the phrase is the same; update the tests with the full text.

The sixth, tests. In the interface tests add checks in rubles: 100 rubles for three give two transfers of 33,33 ₽, and mutual debts 700 for 300 give one transfer of 400,00 ₽. In the transfer tests add a minimality check on pseudo-random sets: your own simple generator with a fixed seed, without new dependencies, 200–500 sets of 2–8 non-zero balances with a zero sum, and an independent reference — a recursive search over splits into zero-sum groups. The number of transfers must equal n minus g of the reference, the balances after the transfers must become zero, the test must run fast, under a second.

At the end run the formatting and make check, it must be green. In the answer write what changed by the points and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here you are. All six fixes are made, make check is green
events.text:
All six fixes are made. Formatting and then make check are green: types, linter, 130 tests and the build. Nothing is committed. The new check on random sets together with the whole transfer test file takes about 0.4 seconds.

One source of truth: I chose the variant with a field in the transfer plan. The plan got the number of participants in the calculation, the calculation itself fills it; the filter in the summary section is removed, the section takes the number from the plan. The expectations in the tests are extended, a check of this number is added to the test about zero balances. The array of notes is now set by one conditional expression without push. The note text about kopecks is replaced with the new one, the copy of this text in the interface tests is updated. The magic number got a named constant with a comment and a function that computes the bit number. The third branch of the phrase about the number of transfers got the new text, the test of the full text is updated; the interface test checks only the beginning of the phrase, it is the same as before.

Tests: two new in the interface — 100 rubles for three give two transfers of 33,33 ₽, mutual debts 700 for 300 give one transfer of 400,00 ₽. In the transfer tests a new block about minimality: own generator with a fixed seed, 400 sets of 2–8 non-zero balances, an independent recursive reference. Checked are the equality of the number of transfers to n minus g, the number of participants in the calculation and the zeroing of the balances, as well as that the sample has sets with several groups, otherwise the test would check nothing.

There are no deviations from the request.

events.line: Accepted. I will check the 14 criteria and the edge cases
events.text:
Check task 2 of the split-bill project against the done criteria. The changes are not committed, they lie in the working copy, task 1 was committed earlier. Tests lie next to the code, DOM tests with the jsdom environment mark, a test checks behavior. Experiments that break the code do only in a copy in a temporary directory. In the working copy change only tests.

Task: calculating the debts with the minimal number of transfers (an exact search over subsets up to 16 non-zero balances, beyond the limit a greedy one with a flag that the minimum is not guaranteed; a transfer plan with a minimality flag and the number of participants in the calculation), tests for the edge cases and a clear explanation in the summary section.

Done criteria. make check is green. Balances 300, 200, minus 200, minus 300 give exactly two transfers. One paid for three — two transfers of 300 rubles. Mutual debts 500 for 500 — no transfers, both are "settled"; 700 for 300 — one transfer of 400 rubles. 100 rubles for three — shares 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33, the sum of the transfers adds up to the kopeck; 0.01 ruble for two — one transfer of 0.01 or "settled". After the transfers all balances are zero, every transfer is positive and between different people. Zero expenses — empty transfers and only the hint without the block "How it is calculated". Exactly at the limit — 8 transfers, the minimality flag; one above — the balances become zero, no more than n minus 1 transfers, the flag is false. A repeated call gives the same result, a frozen input does not change. A non-zero sum is an exception. In the interface for "Ann paid 900 for three" the total, the rows per participant and the phrase about two transfers and three people are visible; for "Ann 300 for Ben, Clara 200 for Eve" — "2 transfers instead of the usual 3" and four people. The note about kopecks is there for 100 rubles for three and absent for 900.

Check the edge cases: one participant with an expense on themselves; a participant without expenses in the breakdown; very large amounts around a billion rubles without loss of precision. If possible, run the scenario "Ann paid 900 for three" in the browser: Chromium is preinstalled, a build, the preview and Playwright from a temporary directory are needed, without new dependencies in the project.

events.line: Checks passed: 14 criteria, I added 7 tests
events.text:
CHECKS PASSED. After formatting and my fixes make check is green: types, linter, 137 tests (was 130) and the build. There are no defects in the code.

By the criteria. Balances 300, 200, minus 200, minus 300 give exactly two needed transfers with the minimality flag and the number of participants in the calculation 4. One paid for three — two transfers of a third each, the same is seen in the interface. Mutual debts 500 for 500 and 700 for 300 are covered both in the calculation and in the interface: for the first one "All settled", both are "settled", the phrase "why this many" is absent; for the second one a transfer of 400,00 ₽. Kopecks are covered: 100 rubles for three with transfers of 33,33 and 0.01 ruble for two for both payers. The balances after the transfers are zero, the amounts are integer and positive, the recipient does not match the debtor; this is checked by the general check and the test on 400 random sets, where the number of transfers is compared with the reference. Zero expenses give empty transfers and the minimality flag, the interface keeps the hint. The limit and the limit plus one, repeatability, immutability of the frozen input and the exception on a non-zero sum are checked. The breakdown "Ann paid 900 for three" is checked by a test and by hand in Chromium through the build, the preview and Playwright without new dependencies: the total, the rows per participant and the phrase about two transfers and three people are visible. The phrase "instead of the usual 3" and the note about kopecks are confirmed by tests. The script output after removing the expense in my run was cut off by output truncation, but the return to the hint is visible in the script itself.

Edge cases: I added the missing tests, all pass. In the transfer tests a new block: one participant with an expense on themselves, a bill of about a billion rubles without loss of precision, large balances in the exact search, a participant without expenses. In the interface tests three new: one participant with an expense on themselves, a participant without expenses with the row "settled", a billion rubles for two with a transfer of 500 000 000,00 ₽. I did not change the code, the fixes are only in tests.
